title: Heroes of Adventure - Spotlight for Free RPG Day 2023
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GJRAN3_x8U4

Daniel (@dungeondive) posts a surprise Saturday episode for Free RPG Day 2023, spotlighting Heroes of Adventure — a free three-book system by the Nameless Designer, available on itch.io with a four-page core-rules PDF alongside the full player's handbook, referee guide and monster compendium.

Mechanically it's a roll-high d20 game with one distinctive turn: instead of static bonuses, skill and attribute proficiency grant you a bonus die — d4 through d12 — added to the d20. Swingier, but there's pleasure in rolling a handful. Characters have agility, command, fortitude, sense, strength and will, plus piety as a currency for divine favour, equipment slots instead of encumbrance, and an unusually long class list running from adventurer and beastmaster through swashbuckler, warlock and zealot. The setting chapter details the Fallen Lands with a two-page hex map you can ignore wholesale if you have your own world.

Daniel's real recommendation is the referee guide, and he says plainly it's the chapter a soloist should print even if they never play the system: generators for settlements, factions, districts, rumours, quests, adventure sites and themes, hazards, traps, puzzles, treasure and artifacts. The Dusky Dragon Inn book of pre-generated NPCs adds random encounter tables sorted by class and race, which he's not seen before.

----

Daniel treats a free game's GM guide as a toolkit to strip for parts rather than a system to adopt. Is that the highest compliment you can pay an RPG book, or a slightly guilty one?
